result:
The proposed answer, 2b + 2, cannot be correct.

A set of n = g + b distinct integers has diameter at least n − 1 = g + b − 1. For large g, this exceeds 2b + 2, so the diameter cannot be 2b + 2. The condition g ≥ (7/4)(b^{3/2} − b) + 1 allows g to be arbitrarily large, so the value must depend on g.

A concrete check with b = 1: the arithmetic progression {0, 1, …, g} has size g + 1. Difference 1 occurs g times, and every larger difference occurs fewer times, so it is a g-Golomb ruler of diameter g. The formula gives 2b + 2 = 4, which fails for any g > 4.

The proposed solution also gives no real derivation. It guesses at the form of the bound without justification.

VERDICT: REJECT
